1.reason: Neither/nor agrees with the nearer subject (sisters -> were); past 'started' requires 'drove'.

2.reason: Plural possessive 'teams'' for three teams; possessive 'its' has no apostrophe.

3.reason: 'Grandpa' used as a name is capitalized; 'my uncle' after a possessive is not.

4.reason: A quoted fragment worked into the sentence stays lowercase; a quoted full sentence after 'added,' is capitalized.

5.reason: Correlative pairs are not only...but also and either...or.

6.reason: Middle Ages is a named era; 'sixteenth century' is lowercase in Chicago, AP and MLA.

7.reason: A tag question is set off by a comma and the sentence ends with a question mark.

8.reason: No comma between the last coordinate adjective and the noun; 'children's' for an irregular plural.

9.reason: Relative adverbs: 'the week when', 'the cabin where'; 'which' cannot introduce clauses with no gap.

10.reason: 'long, exhausting' are coordinate (comma); 'two tall pine' are cumulative (no comma).

11.reason: Languages (English) are capitalized; general subjects (geography) are not.

12.reason: Opening modifier must attach to Talia; 'although' does not take 'but'.

13.reason: No comma after a parenthetical between subject and verb; 'which had won' is nonrestrictive and is set off by paired commas.

14.reason: 'who finished...early' is restrictive (no commas); 'who runs the school garden' is nonrestrictive and must be closed.

15.reason: Proper adjectives Japanese/Canadian are capitalized; 'garden' is a common noun here.

16.reason: Object case 'me'; 'themselves' is standard, 'theirselves' is nonstandard.

17.reason: No shift from 'students' to 'you'; object of 'for' takes 'us sixth graders'.

18.reason: The American Southwest is a named region; 'east' as a direction of travel is lowercase.

19.reason: Past perfect needs the participle 'eaten'; the narrative stays in past ('was reading').

20.reason: 'Avenue' is part of a street name; 'small lake' is a common noun.

21.reason: Comma after the introductory subordinate clause; semicolon joins two independent clauses (B is a comma splice).

22.reason: Counterfactual 'I wish I were' and past-perfect 'if I had practiced'; D's 'was' appears in descriptive dictionaries as informal usage, but school grammar and Chicago/AP formal usage want 'were', so I'm not counting D as an accepted alternative (my cold pass listed it as second_defensible).

23.reason: Series commas after each item; no comma between the compound subject and 'were'. All options keep the serial comma, so AP vs Chicago doesn't split it.

24.reason: Title case: short article 'the' lowercase mid-title, verb 'Was' capitalized. AP, Chicago, MLA and APA agree.
